hook: Explicit restricted isometries now reach sparsity m^(2/3), beating the old m^(1/2) barrier.
summary: The authors build explicit matrices with the restricted isometry property at sparsity k near m^(2/3), using a strongly regular graph, Gershgorin's circle theorem and an incidence result of Zahl. They also show the Gram-matrix-magnitude technique's barrier is m^(2/3), not m^(1/2). Sparsity remains below the m level that random matrices reach.
title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
